results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues
results.summary: Focuses on dropouts and disconnections in live setups. Four checks: device/OS/app up to date, iOS performance (RAM, background apps), the USB connection (named as the most common cause in MultiOut setups), and the audio connection (Auto Pan splitter cable, class-compliant interfaces). The article does not cover no-sound, output selection, Bluetooth, sample rate, or mono/stereo settings.

steps.text: Check the device is supported (supported devices list for iOS, iPadOS, macOS). On the oldest supported iOS generation, Multi-Outs and MIDI Cue editing are limited.
Confirm the OS is up to date and that Playback support for it is confirmed (see the OS compatibility article). Update Playback from the iOS or Mac App Store.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: iOS performance: clear RAM, force-close all background apps before opening Playback, and do not multitask during a live performance.
USB adapter: an official Apple adapter is required (Lightning to USB3 or USB-C to USB3; both allow simultaneous charging).
USB cable length: max 16 feet for USB 2.0, 3 meters (9 feet) for USB 3.0. Keep the digital USB run short and use longer analog runs (XLR, 1/4") from the interface to DI boxes and the console.
Powered USB extension cables: base cable must respect the limits above; the active repeater needs external power; max extender length 25 m (USB 2.0) or 15 m (USB 3.0).
Powered USB hub: must be powered, no more than 7 USB accessory ports, and only one audio interface connected at a time so Playback sends audio to the correct device.
Auto Pan splitter cable: use a high-quality cable with as few adaptors as possible.
Audio interface: Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces; check the tested supported devices list on multitracks.com.
If issues persist, contact MultiTracks support.

results.title: Why is Playback not sending audio out of my Behringer U-Phoria Audio Interface?
results.summary: Covers the UMC404HD and UMC1820. Multi-output through an interface requires a Pro/Premium subscription. The UMC404HD needs a powered USB hub to be powered properly, and on iPhone/iPad the device's master volume controls the level Playback sends to the interface.

steps.text: Confirm you have the right cables, adapters, and hardware to connect Playback to the interface (see the USB interface connection article).
UMC404HD only: connect through a powered USB hub; the hub powers the interface.
iPhone/iPad: after connecting, turn the iOS device's master volume to maximum, since it directly controls the volume out of Playback into the interface.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Download Errors
results.summary: Covers four named download error messages in Playback (Error Authorizing, Audio Files Missing, Insufficient Storage, generic Download Error) plus a catch-all. MultiTracks says download errors are rare and asks users who see the same error repeatedly to report it through the website chat. The article does not name a platform; it refers only to 'the device' and 'the Playback app'.

steps.text: 'Error Authorizing': the download failed a security check (your network may be blocking Playback from verifying the device). Follow the separate article 'Playback Download Error (Download Unauthorized)'.
'Audio Files Missing': tap Try Again at least three times. On the third attempt Playback runs a different recovery routine automatically.

'Audio Files Missing' (if three attempts fail on a song you recently downloaded in past setlists): open the setlist menu, scroll to the bottom, and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device'. Last resort only: it removes all local downloads and every current setlist must be downloaded again.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Insufficient Storage': remove past setlists with 'Delete all setlists from device' at the bottom of the setlist menu. If the error persists, check the device's storage; it may be too full. A typical song is roughly 40 MB to 1 GB, so a full setlist can be several GB.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic): tap Try Again at least two times. If it continues and you are short on time, use Contact Support in the About tab of Playback Settings, then try the quick fixes.
Quick fix 1 - remove and re-add the song: tap Edit, tap the red minus icon on the song, tap '+ Add Song', find the song again, and load it.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Quick fix 2 - download in another key and transpose locally: before loading, change the song's key in song settings to a key close to the one you need; after the download, open song settings in edit mode and change the key back.

Quick fix 3 - clear local data (last resort): contact support first from the About tab, then open the setlist menu (top-right) and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device' at the bottom. All setlists must be redownloaded afterward.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Any other error: contact MultiTracks.com through the website messenger or 'Contact Support' in the About tab of the Playback app.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Setting up Audio and MIDI
results.text:
There are two main ways to send audio out of Playback.

· Auto Pan: Send click and tracks from Playback using the headphone port without any additional audio hardware. Learn how to use Auto Pan with Playback.

· MultiOuts: With a Premium subscription, Playback can send up to 32 outputs can be accessed using compatible audio devices.

Note: For more info on audio routing see:
- 📖Setting up Playback with a sound system
- 📖Connecting to a USB Interface
- 📖Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Live Performance > Tracks/Buses Mixer: Controlling Your Tracks
results.text:
Reference Track Fader and controls

- The reference track is muted by default.
- Soloing the reference track with the circle "S" button will solo the reference track and mute all tracks, including the click and guide.
- Tapping on the "reference" track name will unmute the reference track, and mute all instrument tracks, but keep the click and guide track with the reference.

Master Fader

Take full control of all audience-facing audio with the master track fader. This fader controls the overall volume output of all instrument tracks + buses, as well as the pad player.

Reminder: The master fader volume is globally set by default. For song specific master volume, enable this in General Settings.

- Tip: Do you need to perform a factory reset of Playback for any reason? Triple-Tap the master fader label to initiate a factory reset, wiping all downloaded data and logging out.

steps.text: The reference track is muted by default.
Soloing the reference track with the circle "S" button will solo the reference track and mute all tracks, including the click and guide.
Tapping on the "reference" track name will unmute the reference track, and mute all instrument tracks, but keep the click and guide track with the reference.
Tip: Do you need to perform a factory reset of Playback for any reason? Triple-Tap the master fader label to initiate a factory reset, wiping all downloaded data and logging out.
steps.caution: Changing this setting takes effect immediately and can cut audio for a moment.
